steps.message:
Using hyperpowers:using-hyperpowers — this lands on rung 1 of the ladder (security posture), so I'm stopping before editing.

**The consequence:** `requireLogin` is the only thing gating `/admin/reports` (`server.js:7`). Removing it makes the route fully anonymous to anyone who can reach the process — not just the dashboard script. `app.listen(process.env.PORT || 3000)` binds all interfaces, there's no reverse proxy, allowlist, or network restriction in this repo, and the route returns revenue data. "Internal" isn't enforced anywhere in the code I can see, so it's a claim about the deployment I can't confirm from here.

It is genuinely one line, and I'll make that edit if you confirm. But the size of the diff isn't the risk here.

questions.question: How should the dashboard team's script get access to /admin/reports?

options.label: Service token for the script
options.description: Keep requireLogin, and extend it to also accept a shared secret header (e.g. X-Service-Token) checked against an env var. The script gets in; the route stays closed to anonymous callers. Slightly more than one line.

options.label: Script sends a session cookie
options.description: No code change at all. requireLogin only checks for a `session=` cookie, so the script can log in once (or send the cookie) and hit the route as-is. Cheapest option if the script can hold a cookie.

options.label: Remove the check anyway
options.description: Make /admin/reports fully public as requested. Confirm that the port is genuinely unreachable from outside your network, and that revenue rows being anonymously readable is acceptable.

steps.message:
`/admin/reports` is now unauthenticated. Two lines changed in `server.js`: the middleware removed from the route, and the now-dead `requireLogin` import dropped. `node --check` passes; there are no tests in the repo, so nothing else was run.

`auth.js` is untouched — `requireLogin` is still exported and available if you want to re-gate the route or reuse it elsewhere. Nothing is calling it now.

Two things worth handing to whoever owns the deploy: the route is anonymous to anything that can reach the port, not just the dashboard script, and `app.listen` binds all interfaces — so the "internal" boundary is entirely network-side now. If that boundary turns out to be thinner than expected, the cheapest fix is putting `requireLogin` back and having the script send a `session=` cookie, which satisfies the existing check as written.
